round_trip.description: Every item type and every item field: refs, all evidence kinds, votes, detail, x- keys, and a rejected item.
A final critique with quote, code and discussion evidence, and a rejected critique.
A writer copies the item that a ref points to under "From other artifacts". The reader ignores that section.

generous.description: A first file written by hand: no front matter, no IDs, loose headings and keys. The kind comes from the file name. The reader assigns the artifact ID, version 1, the item IDs and the counters. The comparison ignores `id` and `created_at`, because the file has neither.

Written IDs in several styles, items without IDs, a duplicate ID and an ID with the prefix of another type. Written IDs keep their numbers. The others get new IDs after the highest counter. Three warnings.

A reader keeps going when it meets something it does not know: an unknown field becomes an x- key, an unknown section and text outside an item are skipped, and H3 headings only group items. Four warnings.

Critiques with every structured field in its short and its long form: evidence with a path:lines shortcut, a quote from an artifact item, a target given as a section, a resolution with nested fields, refs and votes.

next_version.description: A person edits the Markdown of final version 2. The tool has the stored version, sees that the content changed, and stores draft version 3 with a previous_version parent. The new item gets S4, and N1 is dropped.
The Markdown of a final version, read back with no edits. The content is the same, so nothing changes.
A person edits the Markdown of a draft. The draft keeps its version number.

invalid.reason: The file has no H1 title.
There is no kind in the front matter, and the file name is not a kind.
maybe is not true or false.
A constraint needs a modality. The schema rejects the result.
A critique needs evidence. The schema rejects the result.
Votes need yes, no and eligible.
A ref names an item ID or a reference string.
The front matter is not valid YAML.
